summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS function, which retrieves local logs from a Snowpark Container Services job container. The feature is not in production and is available only to selected accounts. The page covers the syntax, required and optional arguments, return value, a usage note that only the job's creator can access the logs, and a sample query with output.
one_line: Snowflake reference for SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS, which retrieves logs from a Snowpark Container Services job container.
key_facts: SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS retrieves local logs from a Snowpark Container Services job container.
The SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS feature is not in production and is available only to selected accounts.
The required arguments are job_uuid and container_name.
job_uuid is the Snowflake-assigned UUID of the job, found using the EXECUTE SERVICE instructions.
container_name is the container name as specified in the job specification file.
number_of_most_recent_lines is an optional argument giving the number of most recent log lines to retrieve.
By default, SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS returns up to 100 KB of the most recent log lines.
The function returns a string of newline-separated log entries from the specified job container.
Only the user who created the job can access the logs from the job container.
The example calls SYSTEM$GET_JOB_LOGS with the job UUID '01acc747-0000-60c0-0000-0e99001fd07a' and the container name 'main'.
The sample output shows log lines from a job named job-tutorial, including 'Job started' and 'Job finished' entries at INFO level.
The sample job connected with database TUTORIAL_DB, schema DATA_SCHEMA, warehouse TUTORIAL_WAREHOUSE, and role TEST_ROLE.
